This MySQL 5 Development Part 2 course continues the introduction to MySQL we began with Part 1. But in Part 2, we now begin working with commands that are used to change the contents of the tables in our database. We also explore various ways of building more complex queries, including command options that allow us to address more than one table in a single command. While this is still an introductory course, we are now exploring tools that let us handle more complex operations and build more sophistication into our MySQL database systems. The topics we cover in Part 2 include inserting/updating/deleting data, subqueries, joins, transactions, table and row locking, stored procedures and functions, triggers and events, indexes, and more. We have tried to keep the examples in the lessons as simple as possible to illustrate them most effectively, but the further study exercises are more realistic as to how these tools are used in practice. To begin learning today, simply click on the movie links.

datafield.subfield: Study of oil palm mesocarp reuse for biopest product /
Project paper (Bachelor of Civil Engineering) -- Universiti Malaysia Pahang - 2007

Oil palm mesocarp is one of the components that produce palm oil. It can be reuse as one of the potential BIOPEST product for termite control. Instead for being just a waste, a study is carried out to prove that it can be reuse in order to reduce environmental pollution. Nowadays, termite problems occurred everywhere and cause a lot of damages. The objectives of the study are to produce oil palm mesocarp as one of the artificial bait product in order to attract termites. Sample of mesocarp is taken at the Felda Palm Oil Industry Sdn Bhd at Lepar Hilir, Gambang, Kuantan. First, mesocarp itself without any additional sugar or chemicals is divided into 5 samples and placed at study field, at Seri Damai Tengah Village, Jaya Gading, Kuantan. The duration is 3 days and the observations are made 3 times. Then, samples preparation is made in the laboratory. 9 samples of mesocarp are prepared in 9 perforated containers and labeled from 1 to 9. 350 gram of sugar is dissolved in 700 ml of water to produce sucrose dissolvent of 50 % concentration. The dissolvent is then divided into 9 different concentrations and is diluted in 200 ml distilled water. Different concentration of sucrose is added into 9 samples of the meso carp and they are placed at different locations in the store room at the study field. This method is repeated 6 times. The results show that mesocarp itself cannot attract termites at all while the sucrose mesocarp can attract numbers of termites. The highest numbers of termites attracted is sample which contains 40 ml of sucrose that is 10 % concentration. This proved that termite's interest is cellulose. The cost of mesocarp with average weight is 30 gram and the concentration of 10 % is only RM 0.11. From the study, mesocarp can be reuse as to be produce as one of the environmental friendly product in order to control termite problems beside decrease the environmental pollution. Sugar is added to increase sucrose level in mesocarp so that termites are attracted to it. In the other words, it can be produce as one of the artificial bait for termite control with a cheaper cost. -Author
Empty Fruit Bunch (EFB) as a natural raw material for artificial bait of isoptera sp (termites) /
Project paper (Bachelor of Civil Engineering) -- Universiti Malaysia Pahang - 2007

Oil palm empty fruit bunch (EFB) is a lignocellulose waste from the oil palm mill. It is generates during the process of extraction of palm oil from palm fruit EFB has a great potential to become a natural raw material for artificial bait of isoptera sp (termites). The objective of the present study was to evaluate the potential of the EFB as a natural solid resource medium as artificial bait to eliminate termites and to determine the composition of the EFB as an attraction to termites. There are two types of EFB fiber used as bait material in this experiment which are EFB fiber before shredded and EFB fiber after shredded. During the experiment, the EFB fiber was divided into two categories to attract the termites which are treated with solution AntiPestI and without treated with solution AntiPestI. Solution AntiPestI is one type of slow-acting chemical. It was found that only EFB fiber before shredded and without treated with solution AntiPestI able to attract the termites within three days. Result analysis reveals that EFB fiber contains 34.1±1.5% of cellulose, 67±1.5% of glucose, 32±1.8% ofpentose, 32±1.8% of hexose, 33.7±2.6% of xylose and 16±2% of ethanol. The moisture content of the EFB without shredded is 56.1 % and the moisture content of the shredded EFB is only 18.3%. The sample used in experiment contains O.7695g/L of oil and O.8415g/L of glucose for one sample. The presence of these compositions is the most important reason the make the EFB fiber able to attract termites. EFB fiber has a great potential to become artificial bait for termites. It is an effective alternative way to reduce the production of solid waste in Malaysia as well as to reduce the building damaged by termites and also decrease the environmental issues created by the abundance of EFB. -Author
